items.name: fix_a
items.direction: Narrate this as a popular, witty long-form history YouTube documentary about India. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller: relaxed and conversational, curious, lightly funny, with a short comic pause before each punchline and before chapter turns. Chars voices funny cartoon characters (a cheeky time-traveller, city inspectors, brick-makers, engineers, kings, emperors, sultans, merchants, soldiers): short, punchy, expressive, following the bracketed style tags. Pronounce Indian names and places naturally, the way an Indian speaker would. VOICE IDENTITY (most important): the Narrator is always the same person: a low, warm baritone documentary host. Keep his voice identity and natural speaking pitch the same from the first line to the last, so it never sounds like a different or younger narrator. Emotion is welcome: show it freely through emphasis, energy, pace, louder and softer moments and dramatic pauses, as a real storyteller would. Never whisper or go breathy.
lines: And into the north, through the mountain passes, came new arrivals once again.
In twelve oh six, Ghori's general Qutb ud-Din Aibak became the first ruler of the Delhi Sultanate. He began the tallest brick minaret in the world: the Qutb Minar.
Around the same time, according to later chronicles, raiders led by Bakhtiyar Khalji attacked Nalanda, and the great university was ruined.
For the next three hundred years, five different dynasties would rule from Delhi.
One sultan, Alauddin Khalji, beat back several Mongol invasions. Unlike China, Persia and Russia, India was never conquered by the Mongols.
He also tried something very modern: price controls. He fixed the price of grain, horses, cloth, even slaves in the markets of Delhi, and punished cheating shopkeepers harshly.
In fifteen twenty-six, a young prince from Central Asia rode down from Kabul. He had lost his homeland more than once. He was looking for a new one.
His great-great-great-grandfather was Timur. And on his mother's side, he was descended from Genghis Khan.
The Golden Bird was free. Now it had to learn to fly again.
